definition: In historical psychology and psychiatry, degeneration referred to a supposed mental or nervous decline viewed as a backward movement in human development. The term was used broadly and imprecisely for a mixed group of people thought to show inherited nervous weakness, mental abnormalities, eccentricity, criminality, or vulnerability to insanity.
